content: Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is recommended. Similarly, famotidine decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH, and the same caution applies. To minimize interaction, separate gefitinib and H2-antagonist doses by at least 6 hours. Magnesium hydroxide reduces gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to oral forms of both agents, and close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate and gemifloxacin can also reduce each other's levels through the same mechanism. Separate their administration by 2 hours. Gentamicin decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance and reduces calcium carbonate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. Famotidine increases glipizide levels or effects by raising gastric pH, as does calcium carbonate. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and caution with monitoring is advised. Glucagon intranasal increases magnesium hydroxide levels by reducing renal clearance, but the clinical significance is unknown. Famotidine increases glyburide levels or effects by raising gastric pH, as does calcium carbonate. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and caution with monitoring is advised. Hydrochlorothiazide increases calcium carbonate levels by reducing renal clearance and decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. These are minor interactions with unknown significance. Hydrocortisone reduces calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination, a minor interaction with unknown significance. Calcium carbonate decreases ibandronate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, as does magnesium hydroxide. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate reduces imidapril effects through an unspecified mechanism. Indapamide increases calcium carbonate levels by reducing renal clearance and decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. These are minor interactions with unknown significance. Famotidine decreases indinavir levels or effects by increasing gastric pH, as does calcium carbonate. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and alternative drugs should be considered. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib (DSC) by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, as does magnesium hydroxide. Famotidine also reduces infigratinib levels. If co-administration with acid-reducing agents cannot be avoided, administer infigratinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after an H2-antagonist. Famotidine decreases iron dextran complex levels or effects by increasing gastric pH, as does calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate also reduces iron dextran complex levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, while iron dextran complex increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and close monitoring is recommended. Famotidine decreases iron sucrose levels or effects by increasing gastric pH, as does calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate also reduces iron sucrose levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, while iron sucrose increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and close monitoring is recommended. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases famotidine levels or effects through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Calcium carbonate reduces isoniazid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, and isoniazid decreases calcium carbonate levels through the same mechanism. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and close monitoring is recommended. Isotretinoin increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Calcium carbonate reduces isradipine effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, and close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate decreases itraconazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, as does famotidine by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to oral forms, and alternative drugs should be considered. Calcium carbonate also reduces ketoconazole levels through the same mechanisms, and alternative drugs are recommended. Calcium carbonate reduces labetalol effects through an unspecified mechanism and decreases its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours, and close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate reduces lactulose effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism, and close monitoring is recommended. Lanthanum carbonate interacts with magnesium hydroxide and calcium carbonate through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. Calcium carbonate decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels through an unspecified mechanism, as does famotidine. Ledipasvir solubility decreases as pH increases, so drugs that raise gastric pH are expected to reduce its levels. H2-receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. Magnesium hydroxide reduces levofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, as does calcium carbonate. Separate their administration by 2 hours, and close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases levothyroxine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 4 hours, and close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate increases the effects of lily of the valley through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Calcium carbonate increases lisdexamfetamine levels or effects through passive renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine, and close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate reduces lisinopril effects through an unspecified mechanism, and close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate and manganese reduce each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours, and close monitoring is recommended. Mannitol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Mefloquine increases famotidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Calcium carbonate increases memantine levels or effects through passive renal tubular reabsorption in basic urine, and close monitoring is recommended. Famotidine decreases mesalamine levels or effects by increasing gastric pH, while calcium carbonate interacts with mesalamine through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. Mestranol decreases magnesium hydroxide levels through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Famotidine increases metformin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Calcium carbonate reduces methscopolamine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours, and close monitoring is recommended. Methyclothiazide increases calcium carbonate levels by reducing renal clearance and decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. These interactions are minor, with unknown significance. Famotidine decreases methylphenidate effects by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption, as does calcium carbonate. Since the release of methylphenidate extended-release capsules (Ritalin LA) is pH-dependent, co-administration of antacids or acid suppressants could alter its release. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Methylprednisolone reduces calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Metolazone decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance and increases calcium carbonate levels by reducing renal clearance. These interactions are minor, with unknown significance. Calcium carbonate reduces metoprolol effects through an unspecified mechanism and decreases its levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours, and close monitoring is recommended. Famotidine and mifepristone increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
